## What This Code Does

This demo creates a diverse agent population and analyses statistical properties including coefficient of variation, skewness, kurtosis, entropy, and Gini coefficients. It generates individual agent trajectories to show how resilience, affect, resources, and stress evolve, and computes correlation matrices across agent attributes using multiple population configurations.

## Mock Model

::: {#mock .cell execution_count=2}
``` {.python .cell-code}
class MockGrid:
    def __init__(self, w=10, h=10):
        self.width, self.height = w, h
    def get_neighbors(self, pos, include_center=False):
        return []

class MockModel:
    def __init__(self, seed=None, w=10, h=10):
        self.grid = MockGrid(w, h)
        self.agents = []
        self.rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
        self.running = True
    def register_agent(self, agent):
        self.agents.append(agent)
```
:::


## Generate Diverse Population

::: {#generate .cell execution_count=3}
``` {.python .cell-code}
config = {
    "initial_resilience_mean": 0.6, "initial_resilience_sd": 0.18,
    "initial_affect_mean": 0.1, "initial_affect_sd": 0.3,
    "initial_resources_mean": 0.7, "initial_resources_sd": 0.15,
    "stress_probability": 0.4, "coping_success_rate": 0.55, "subevents_per_day": 3,
}

n_agents = 200
agents = []
for i in range(n_agents):
    model = MockModel(seed=1000 + i)
    agent = Person(model, config)
    agents.append(agent)

resilience = np.array([a.resilience for a in agents])
affect = np.array([a.affect for a in agents])
resources = np.array([a.resources for a in agents])
pss10 = np.array([a.pss10 for a in agents])
```
:::


## Diversity Metrics

::: {#metrics .cell execution_count=4}
``` {.python .cell-code}
def _entropy(hist):
    p = hist / hist.sum()
    p = p[p > 0]
    return -np.sum(p * np.log(p))

def diversity_metrics(values, name):
    mean, std = np.mean(values), np.std(values, ddof=1)
    cv = std / abs(mean) if mean != 0 else 0
    skew = pd.Series(values).skew()
    kurt = pd.Series(values).kurtosis()
    unique = len(set(np.round(values, 4)))
    hist, _ = np.histogram(values, bins=20)
    ent = _entropy(hist)
    print(f"{name}: mean={mean:.3f} sd={std:.3f} cv={cv:.3f} "
          f"skew={skew:.3f} kurt={kurt:.3f} unique={unique}/{n_agents} entropy={ent:.3f}")

diversity_metrics(resilience, "Resilience")
diversity_metrics(affect, "Affect")
diversity_metrics(resources, "Resources")
diversity_metrics(pss10, "PSS-10")
```

## Why This Matters for the Simulation

Agent diversity is essential for emergent population dynamics. If the agent pool lacks variation, the model cannot capture the heterogeneous responses to stress observed in real populations. Diversity metrics (Gini, entropy, CV, skewness) quantify how well the initialization produces realistic spread, while correlation matrices validate that theoretical relationships between attributes (e.g., resilience ↔ PSS-10) are present from the start.
